Computational Astrophysics

Sachi Weerasooriya

I work on modeling galaxies for future surveys, such as Roman, with a focus on accurate modeling of emission lines and calibrating models using the Semi-Analytic Model Galacticus. My research interests also include modeling dwarf galaxies and exploring the impact of major mergers on stellar streams and their properties. I am passionate about connecting science with art.

Postdoctoral Researcher, NASA Open Universe Project · Carnegie Observatories, Pasadena, CA · Ph.D. Texas Christian University (Advisor: Dr. Mia Sauda Bovill)

Recent Updates

Research & News

Papers, talks, and highlights from ongoing work.

2026
In Review
The Curious Case of Centaurus A: On the Subject of Quenched Satellites

A follow-up to the Cen A satellites paper, disentangling environmental vs. internal quenching pathways in the Centaurus A group using Galacticus.

Jun 2026
Paper
Dancing Streams In Merging Halos: Stellar Streams in a MW–LMC-like Merger — Open Journal of Astrophysics 9, 26

We show that the LMC’s infall strongly perturbs stellar stream tracks in a Milky Way analogue, producing apparent gaps that mimic dark-matter substructure signatures.

2026
Talk
AAS 248 Special Session — “May the Flux Be With You”

Presented physically motivated atomic emission line models built in Galacticus, targeting Roman, Euclid, and LSST-era near-IR spectroscopic surveys.

Fall 2025
Outreach
Art & Science Exhibit — Carnegie Observatories Open House

Organised the Art & Science Exhibit at the Carnegie Observatories annual public open house, Pasadena, CA.

2025
Talk
Three invited talks — U. Arizona, U. Peradeniya (Sri Lanka), Pasadena City College

“Devouring Dwarf Galaxies with Galacticus” — invited seminars on semi-analytic modeling of the Local Volume satellite population.

2025
Paper
DiffstarPop: A Generative Physical Model of Galaxy Star Formation History — arXiv:2510.27604

Co-authored generative model for galaxy SFHs spanning wide-field surveys; contributed dwarf galaxy validation.
